scheme_name: Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/ Kankarej Breed
description:
The Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/Kankrej Breed is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at enhancing the livestock sector in the country.

This scheme was launched in 2014 under the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The primary objective of the scheme is to improve the genetic quality of indigenous cattle breeds such as Gir and Kankrej.

The scheme aims to increase the population of these breeds which are known for their high milk yield and adaptability to local conditions.

The government has set a target to enhance the breeding efficiency of these cattle by providing quality bulls for artificial insemination.

The scheme also aims to increase the income of farmers by improving milk production and quality.

Under this scheme, the government provides financial assistance for the purchase of high-quality bulls.

Farmers can receive up to ₹50,000 for the purchase of a single bull.

This amount is intended to cover the costs associated with acquiring and managing the bulls.

The scheme also includes provisions for the management of bulls to ensure their health and productivity.

Farmers are encouraged to participate in training programs to learn about proper care and management of bulls.

Eligibility for the scheme includes farmers who own a minimum of five cows or buffaloes.

Farmers must also be registered with the local animal husbandry department.

The age limit for applicants is typically between 18 to 60 years.

Income criteria stipulate that the annual income of the farmer should not exceed ₹2 lakh.

The application process involves several steps to ensure transparency and accountability.

Farmers must fill out an application form available at the local animal husbandry office.

They are required to submit documents such as proof of identity, proof of land ownership, and income certificate.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the local animal husbandry officer.

The officer will verify the documents and conduct a field visit if necessary.

If approved, the financial assistance is disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account.

The timeline for the application process typically spans 30 to 45 days from the date of submission.

Disbursement of funds is done in a single installment after approval.

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying at both the state and central levels.

State governments are responsible for the execution of the scheme in their respective regions.

Contact details for the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying can be found on their official website.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote indigenous breeds and improve the livelihoods of rural farmers.

The Gir breed is known for its high milk production capacity which can reach up to 20 liters per day.

Kankrej cattle are also recognized for their resilience and adaptability to harsh climates.

Both breeds are integral to the dairy industry in states like Gujarat and Rajasthan.

The government has also established breeding centers to facilitate the availability of quality bulls.

These centers are equipped with modern facilities for artificial insemination and veterinary care.

The scheme encourages farmers to adopt scientific breeding practices to enhance productivity.

Farmers are also provided with veterinary services to ensure the health of their livestock.

The initiative is expected to contribute significantly to the national milk production targets.

India aims to increase its milk production to over 200 million metric tons by 2025.

The scheme is aligned with the National Livestock Policy which emphasizes sustainable livestock development.

Training programs under the scheme cover topics such as animal husbandry practices and disease management.

The government also conducts awareness campaigns to educate farmers about the benefits of the scheme.

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are carried out to assess its impact on livestock productivity.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the implementation of the scheme.

The scheme has received positive responses from various stakeholders in the agricultural sector.

It is expected to lead to an increase in the income levels of farmers involved in dairy farming.

The initiative also supports the conservation of indigenous cattle breeds which are at risk of extinction.

The government has allocated a budget of ₹100 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the current financial year.

This funding is aimed at supporting the purchase of bulls and enhancing breeding programs.

The scheme is expected to create job opportunities in the rural economy through increased dairy production.

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives to collectively manage the breeding and marketing of milk.

The cooperative model is seen as a way to enhance bargaining power and reduce costs.

The scheme also promotes the use of technology in breeding practices.

Farmers can access information about the scheme through the official website and local offices.

The government has partnered with various NGOs and organizations to promote the scheme.

These partnerships aim to extend the reach of the scheme to remote and underserved areas.

The scheme is a part of the larger framework of rural development initiatives by the Indian government.

It reflects the commitment to improving the livelihoods of farmers and promoting sustainable agriculture.

The success of the scheme will be measured by the increase in the population of Gir and Kankrej breeds.

The government aims to achieve a 20 percent increase in the population of these breeds within five years.

Overall the Scheme for Management and Purchase of Bulls Provided for Breeding of State Gir/Kankrej Breed is a comprehensive initiative aimed at enhancing the livestock sector in India.
